bullets.title: NVDA -5% on CEO Jensen Huang affair/espionage investigation; board launches independent probe
bullets.body: NVIDIA's board initiated an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, described by US intelligence as a suspected Chinese Ministry of State Security asset affiliated with Megaspeed (under export control review). The board states no evidence of IP or national security compromise; Huang remains CEO and committed to cooperate. Republican House members requested a closed-door briefing Nov 18; Polymarket pricing CEO ouster at 17%. Multiple brokers cut or put on hold: Aletheia downgraded to Hold; Citi maintains Buy at $315 PT (~21x C27E).

bullets.title: Semi selloff near capitulation: SOX -28% in 22 days, pricing ~30-35% EPS cuts; buy-side sees trough
bullets.body: The SOX is down 28% over 22 days—one of the largest rolling 1-month drawdowns on record—and now trades at ~10.9-13x 2-year forward P/E, near GFC and 2012-2014 troughs. Multiple strategists (GS, UBS, MS, JPM) characterize the selloff as overdone: GS raised NVDA PT to $300 (11x CY27 EPS $16.70) and AVGO to $540 (13x); UBS notes current prices imply ~30% C27 and ~35% C28 EPS cuts. Hedge funds net sold semis at a 4-sigma pace over the past month, back to July/Liberation Day lows; systematic/CTA selling added ~$80-120B Thursday alone.

bullets.title: Post-midterm data center permitting risk: ~20% of 2028 US DC capacity pushed to 2029; hyperscaler capex forecasts intact
bullets.body: Democratic midterm gains triggered sharp tech selling as Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa pledged to suspend data center approvals pending community protections. Morgan Stanley estimates ~20% of US data center projects (~5GW) shift from 2028 to 2029; ~41% of planned capacity sits in states where governors support a moratorium. Critically, hyperscaler capex forecasts remain unchanged at $1.6T/$1.8T for 2027/2028 (MS), and Goldman expects $1.7T in 2027 (+87% growth). Existing, already-contracted and permitted builds (Oracle's 7GW through May 2028) are largely unaffected; the risk is to unpermitted 2028+ projects.

bullets.title: Hedge fund deleveraging at historic extremes: record tech net selling, L/S net leverage at 3-yr lows
bullets.body: Hedge funds sold tech at the fastest pace on record last week—six straight sessions of AI-stock net selling totaling >$20B. Multi-strat de-grossing was the largest in 20 days since COVID; L/S net leverage fell to 3-year lows (5th largest single-day drop since 2005). Levered ETFs sold ~$60B Thursday and ~$35B the prior Friday. Goldman's vol panic gauge hit 9.57/10, the 3rd largest daily jump ever. QQQ RSI dipped below 30, a level that historically precedes ~4% average rallies over the next five trading days.

bullets.title: JPM strategist Dubravko holds SPX 8,000 YE26 target; momentum unwind seen near end
bullets.body: JPM's Dubravko reiterates a year-end S&P 500 target of 8,000 ($365 EPS at 21.9x), implying ~8.4% upside from Friday's close. The momentum factor (JPMPURE) fell 15.7% over five weeks; AI basket multiples compressed ~35% since May (semis -52%, memory -60%). Momentum crowding reset from 100th percentile to 76th; JPM argues the de-leveraging event is largely done, with QQQ RSI sub-30 and levered ETF exposure below January 2026 levels. Every $100B in AI capex translates to ~$9 in S&P 500 EPS (~2.5% earnings growth).

bullets.title: Two-speed economy: non-tech cyclicals accelerating on Fed easing lag; AI capex slowing to 50% growth in 2027
bullets.body: Multiple macro strategists describe a bifurcated economy: AI/tech is mid-cycle while non-tech (90%+ of GDP) is early-cycle, benefiting from the 2024-2025 Fed easing with a typical 2-year lag. Goods-producing jobs rose 201K over the past year, led by data center/nonres construction. Real consumer spending is tracking ~3% entering 2027, supported by 4.4% nominal compensation growth and 8% real net worth gains. AI capex is expected to slow from ~80% YoY to ~50% in 2027, becoming an incremental headwind rather than a primary driver.

bullets.title: Fed hiking cycle not done: December 25bp hike base case; US core PCE rising to 3.3%
bullets.body: JPMorgan forecasts a 25bp Fed hike in December, with core CPI at 0.23% m/m and US PCE rising to 3.8% in November (core PCE 3.3%). Wolfe projects core PCE peaking at 3.2% YoY end-2026, slowing to 2.5% by end-2027; tariffs, memory shortages, and Iran war added ~100bp to YoY core PCE in 2026. The FOMC is expected to deliver two more hikes (December 2026 and March 2027), taking Fed Funds to 4.25-4.50%. Piper Sandler puts December hike probability above 90%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 3Q26 earnings solid: 31.4-31.7% EPS growth, 77-84% beat rate; tech outperforming at 48% EPS growth
bullets.body: With ~80% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 3Q26 EPS growth is tracking 31.4-31.7% on 14.3-14.4% revenue growth; 77-84% of companies have beaten estimates by an average of 2.7-5.6% (below 5- and 10-year averages of 7.5-8%). The TECH+ sector is growing EPS 48.3% vs the broader market's 31.7%. All 11 sectors show positive revenue and earnings growth. Despite strong results, market reactions have been muted—only 29% of stocks beat implied moves vs 42% historically, per Citi.

bullets.title: Google accelerates TPU releases: TPU 8tx and 8i Max launched for confidential computing and long-context tasks
bullets.body: Google unveiled two new TPU variants (8tx for confidential computing, 8i Max for long-context tasks), accelerating its chip release cadence from one every two years to multiple in 2026. JPM describes these as reconfigured SKUs rather than entirely new silicon, but notes they meaningfully expand the competitive pressure on NVDA/AVGO. AVGO is separately designing a 'Blade Runner' TPU anticipated by JPM. Google Cloud revenue is already up 103% YoY with a $561B backlog; TPU system sales are expected to ramp materially in 2027.

bullets.title: China extends US trade truce to Jan 10; suspends 24% retaliatory tariff and special port fees
bullets.body: China announced a suspension of its additional 24% retaliatory tariff on US goods and special fees on American ships until January 10, extending the existing trade truce. This was flagged by multiple sources as a constructive geopolitical development reducing near-term trade war escalation risk. Separately, Trump characterized military action against Iran as 'highly unlikely' contingent on a 'very strong agreement,' and WTI fell ~1.1% to $89.37 on reduced escalation fears.

bullets.title: AI capex ROI debate intensifying: enterprise adoption slower than expected, monetization lagging spending
bullets.body: An Oppenheimer survey of 449 IT buyers found AI ROI validation is becoming the critical bottleneck for enterprise software spending in 2027; overall IT spend is not accelerating even as AI captures incremental budget share. 22V Research notes AI usage fell quarter-over-quarter with no sector broadening, adoption stalling at the productivity-tool stage rather than driving labor displacement. Anthropic's compute costs are approaching 90% of revenue by Q1-Q2 2027. Morgan Stanley finds 44% of S&P 500 companies now quantify AI financial benefits (up from 32%), but only 26% cite measurable financial impact.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO at ~$1.5T valuation expected before Thanksgiving; roadshow potentially starting this week
bullets.body: Anthropic is pressing ahead with an IPO at approximately $1.5T valuation with the roadshow potentially starting this week, per multiple sources. October ARR exceeded $80B (up from $65-70B in September). The company secured 1.7GW of gas-fired generators for $3.4B and raised $11B at $1.25T valuation in a recent round. 22V puts the IPO probability at 75%+; valuation expectations have moderated from an earlier $2T target.

bullets.title: VIX at 23 vs 15-17 'Normal expansion' regime; 22V sees short-VIX opportunity as AI buildout names stabilize
bullets.body: 22V Research issues a short-VIX and short-Low-Vol factor call with 6.5/10 conviction for the next month, citing the Low-Vol vs High-Vol factor spread at the 99th percentile month-over-month (historically expensive). VIX is at 23 vs a typical 15-17 range in the Normal expansion regime that has persisted since early 2024. S&P 500 Technology NTM EPS changes remain positive since the July selloff, with semis NTM EPS up 6.6% on a monthly median basis. Key risk: another idiosyncratic AI selloff or hot CPI print.

bullets.title: Southeast Asian DC growth pausing; Malaysia halted 49 projects, Thailand delayed 117 on power/water constraints
bullets.body: JPM's semiconductor desk flags a pause in Southeast Asian data center build-out: Malaysia halted 49 projects and Thailand delayed 117 approvals due to power and water constraints. Separately, DRAM supply could effectively halve in 2027 as AI datacenters absorb capacity. These supply-side pressures compound the US permitting delays described above and represent a broader global AI infrastructure bottleneck.

bullets.title: MS and Morgan Stanley see market selloff as clearing event; breadth improving, valuation derating ~19% YTD
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley characterizes the correction as nearing final innings: S&P 500 forward P/E has de-rated ~19% YTD, equal-weight S&P and S&P ex-AI made new all-time highs the same week as the selloff, and credit fundamentals are improving. Manufacturing PMIs remain at cycle highs, jobless claims near record lows, and forward earnings continue rising. 60% of Russell 3000 stocks experienced 20%+ corrections. Piper Sandler sets a year-end SPX target of 7,500 with energy, healthcare, and select financials showing new leadership.

bullets.title: Tech credit spreads doubled since March; ORCL/CRWV CDS widened; hyperscaler FCF negative at AMZN, GOOGL
bullets.body: Tech credit spreads are near +100bps, having doubled since March; ORCL and CRWV CDS widened materially post-election on financing concerns. Amazon and Google FCF turned negative ($35B and $9B respectively) in Q3, and hyperscalers are arguably in a 'prisoner's dilemma' defending legacy businesses. AKAM issued a $2.2B convertible offering partly to fund cloud infrastructure capex. Over $150B of SPV-backed compute financing has been announced for 2027 vs ~$900M currently trading, representing a structural shift in AI financing.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Tech losing leadership; Healthcare, Consumer Staples, Financials now leading on relative strength
bullets.body: Multiple technical and macro strategists confirm a sector rotation underway. Piper Sandler moved Technology to underweight with Financials, Healthcare, and Staples now overweight. Roth's trend model has Technology slipping to underweight. Oppenheimer's Ari Wald upgrades Financial Services to Overweight and downgrades Energy to Market Weight, while adding SPOT, CART, and NET to Trifecta buys. The Russell 1000 Value/Growth ratio broke above two years of resistance, suggesting value rotation with durability.

bullets.title: US core inflation sticky above Fed target; JPM forecasts US PCE 3.8%, core PCE 3.3% for November
bullets.body: JPMorgan's global inflation forecast shows US headline CPI at 3.9% YoY and PCE at 3.8% in November, with core CPI at 2.8% and core PCE at 3.3%—running 50bps+ above the Fed's ~2% speed limit. Tariffs, memory shortages, and the Iran war added ~100bp to YoY core PCE in 2026. Wolfe's 2027 outlook forecasts core PCE peaking at 3.2% year-end 2026 before slowing to 2.5% by end-2027. Baseline core PCE forecasts for the next 3-4 months are described as 'too dovish' given tariff and cost pressures.

bullets.title: MRVL-LITE $115B all-stock deal: accretive to 2028 EPS but raises peak-cycle durability concerns
bullets.body: Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum at ~$115B EV in an all-stock deal was met skeptically by the market—both stocks fell sharply. The industrial logic centers on combining silicon and photonics for integrated scale-up and scale-in optical solutions, with LITE's 5 NPO designs now expected in production 2028-2029 vs prior 2030+. UBS bull case suggests ~14% accretion to C2028 EPS, but Wolfe Research and industry contacts questioned the customer value proposition and raised peak-cycle durability concerns.

bullets.title: October payrolls +165K, well above +70K consensus; labor market broadening; white-collar hiring best since Dec 2024
bullets.body: October nonfarm payrolls came in at +165K vs a +70K consensus, with the unemployment rate falling despite higher labor force participation. It was the best month for white-collar hiring since December 2024; blue-collar hiring remained strong. Average hourly earnings posted 0.4% m/m growth. The report supports JPM's forecast of a December 25bp Fed hike and March 2027 follow-through; initial jobless claims hit a 52-week low. This data point reduces recession risk but reinforces the Fed's tightening path.
